title: Account Review QBR Variations — Growth & Risk Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This working pack contains two compact QBR deck templates (Standard and Enterprise variations) together with speaker notes, a renewal-readiness checklist, a short renewal tracker table (text form), and an outreach cadence + sample email copy. Goal is a lightweight, repeatable QBR that customer success managers (CSMs) can customize quickly for both growth-focused and retention-risk conversations.

How to use this file:
- Choose the deck variation that matches the customer segment (Standard for SMB / mid-market; Enterprise for large strategic accounts).
- Populate the Metrics and Health slides from product dashboards and the account tracker below.
- Use the Risk Signals checklist to decide escalation and playbook steps.
- Copy-paste the slide titles and speaker notes into Google Slides template; keep the "Ask" slide at the end to make renewals explicit.

=== STANDARD DECK (mid-market / expansion-first) ===
Slide 1: Title & Agenda
Speaker notes: 30s opener, remind of partnership goal and timebox, run through three agenda items: wins, metrics, opportunities.

Slide 2: Executive Summary (1 slide)
Speaker notes: 1-2 bullets: ARR impact-to-date, adoption trend, one line ask. Keep it upbeat.

Slide 3: Recent Wins & Use Cases (2-3 bullets + screenshots)
Speaker notes: Share 2 quick customer stories or feature adoptions that moved the needle. Tie to product releases.

Slide 4: Health Metrics Snapshot (table)
Speaker notes: Show 90/30/7 day active usage, requests per minute, token consumption trend, errors rate, key feature adoption. Include one chart showing month-over-month change.

Slide 5: Expansion Opportunities
Speaker notes: Call out top 2 areas for expansion (additional seats, higher concurrency, private deployment). Frame in $ impact.

Slide 6: Risks & Concerns (brief)
Speaker notes: Surface 1-2 friction points: latency spikes, cost noise, integration gaps. Add triage owner.

Slide 7: Action Plan & Timeline (30/60/90)
Speaker notes: Assign owners, success criteria, and next check-in date.

Slide 8: Ask & Renewal Window
Speaker notes: State the renewal date, propose contract term, call out incentives if applicable.

Appendix (optional): billing snapshot, operation runbook link, contact matrix.

=== ENTERPRISE DECK (strategic accounts / multi-stakeholder) ===
Slide 1: Cover + Stakeholders present
Speaker notes: Call out executive sponsor and technical owner; include meeting goals (strategy, risk review, contract alignment).

Slide 2: One-page Strategic Narrative
Speaker notes: How Redwood Inference fits into the customer's product roadmap and cost/latency targets. Link to their OKRs if available.

Slide 3: Adoption & ROI Highlights (detailed)
Speaker notes: Show 6–12 month cumulative metrics: token-volume trends, model variants used, latency percentiles (p50/p90/p99), error budget consumption, cost per 1k tokens.

Slide 4: Reliability & SLOs
Speaker notes: Present uptime, incident summary since last QBR, mitigations, and planned reliability investments (dedicated pools, fallbacks).

Slide 5: Security & Compliance Posture
Speaker notes: Summarize data residency, KMS integrations, audit events, and any outstanding compliance items.

Slide 6: Optimization Opportunities & Cost Controls
Speaker notes: Suggested batching/quantization changes, model routing adjustments, and estimated $ savings. Provide recommended pilot parameters.

Slide 7: Risk Matrix & Escalation Ladder
Speaker notes: Categorize risks (technical, commercial, org) with mitigation owners and SLAs for response.

Slide 8: Contract & Renewal Recommendation (options)
Speaker notes: Present 3 renewal paths: renew-as-is, expand with dedicated capacity, or transition to private deployment. Include recommended next steps and evaluation timeline.

Slide 9: Appendix & Technical Deep-dive (links to tickets/PRs)
Speaker notes: Link to open SRE/infra PRs and model onboarding issues.

=== RENEWAL READINESS CHECKLIST (use before scheduling QBR) ===
- Renewal date captured? (Y/N)
- Current ARR and committed usage logged? (Y/N)
- NPS / CSAT trends attached? (Y/N)
- Any P1/P2 incidents in last 90 days? (describe)
- Active exec sponsor identified? (name)
- Contract governance constraints noted? (procurement timelines, PO rules)
- Proposed renewal options prepared? (Y/N)

=== RENEWAL TRACKER (text table; paste into sheet) ===
Columns: Account | Renewal date | Current ARR | Proposed option | Owner | Exec sponsor | Risk level (Low/Med/High) | Next step
Sample row: Acme Retail | 2025-05-10 | $145k | Dedicated + 12m | Lena Kim | CTO - Jenna Ortiz | Medium | Schedule pricing review

=== RISK SIGNALS (early warning) ===
- Sudden drop in active requests (-20% over 14d)
- Rising p99 latency above SLA for >24h
- Spike in error rate (>1% of requests)
- Procurement delays / legal pushback
- Executive sponsor rotation

=== PLAYBOOK: IF RISK LEVEL = HIGH ===
1) Immediate: open P1 bridge with SRE and CSM (within 2h)
2) 24h: Exec-to-exec note from CSM + AE summarizing impact and remediation plan
3) 72h: Proposal for interim discount / dedicated capacity offer (commercial)
4) 7d: On-site/remote war-room with engineering and product if unresolved

=== OUTREACH CADENCE (2-week example before renewal) ===
- T-14 days: Personalized executive email (see template below)
- T-12 days: CSM scheduling QBR + share draft deck
- T-7 days: Technical deep dive with SRE/architects
- T-3 days: Final pricing/contract alignment with procurement
- T: QBR meeting + close next steps

Sample executive email (short):
Subject: 2025 QBR + renewal discussion — proposed times
Hi [Exec name],
We’re approaching your renewal window on [date]. We’d like to share a short QBR covering usage, ROI, and a few options that could reduce latency and unit cost. Can you join a 30–45 minute session next week?
Best,
[CSM name]

=== ACTION ITEM/OWNER TEMPLATE (paste into tracker) ===
- Action: Share detailed cost breakdown | Owner: Finance lead | Due: 3 business days
- Action: Pilot quantized model for search feature | Owner: Eng Solutions | Due: 30 days
- Action: Exec alignment call scheduled | Owner: AE | Due: 5 business days

Notes / Tips from CSM Practitioners:
- Keep the Executive Summary to one slide; it determines tone.
- For enterprise accounts, include the legal/procurement touchpoints in the agenda so procurement feels included.
- Always surface one small win and one cost-save recommendation. People respond better to quick wins.

Open questions for this pack (to finalize before release):
- Do we want a separate 10-slide version optimized for 20-minute exec briefings?
- Should we include a one-click sheet export from the Console for the Health Metrics snapshot? (linked_artifacts above)
- Agree on standardized risk-level definitions across CSMs?

End of working draft.
